label: Second copy step (input = first original token) in short sequences (L=3/4) whose remaining tokens include m/x/h/e/0/1/v/z
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase at recall_idx==1 (step L+1, where the model's first output, orig(0), is fed back and orig(1) is output). It is almost exclusively in short sequences: L=3 (52% of mass, 7.8% of such steps) and L=4 (46%); L=5 is rare and L>=6 essentially never. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases. Whether it fires depends on the identity of the upcoming tokens orig(1..L-1): m, x, h, e, 0, 1, v, z give the strongest lift as out_tok or next_out (m and x most of all). In L=3 one such token among orig(1), orig(2) is enough; in L=4 it needs two of the three. The input token (orig(0)) matters less, although m as the first token gives the top activations (max ~5.6, e.g. 'm x 0 <DEL> [m] x'). Without the token condition, (recall_idx==1)&(L<=4) has 96% recall but only 18% precision. Adding the token condition gives dev F1 0.70 and mass recall 0.90. What remains looks like graded per-token contributions, not a crisp rule.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=<DEL> (+5.88), orig5=- (+4.41), phase=2 & out_tok=m (+4.03), next_out=x (+3.40), phase=2 & out_tok=x (+3.33), next_out=e (+3.21). Lower it: prev2_tok=p (-3.62), prev2_tok=k (-2.82), orig2=a (-2.80), orig1=k (-2.79).
